It has therefore been postulated that training to the point of concentric muscular failure, regardless of the magnitude of load, ultimately results in the recruitment of the full spectrum of available motor units (33, 45). However, although acknowledging that motor unit activity does increase with fatigue, others claim that lifting very heavy loads results in specific recruitment patterns that are not attainable with light-load training (125).
